notes.title: Polysomnography Report
notes.author: Sleep medicine physician
notes.text:
Polysomnography Report
Date: 11/16/2025
Patient: Shaunna McClure, 66-year-old female

Diagnostic in-laboratory polysomnography performed 11/16/2025. Total apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) 52.8 events/hour. Central and mixed apneas comprised 18% of all events. The study showed disrupted sleep architecture with frequent arousals related to respiratory events. Oxygen saturation levels dropped intermittently during apneas. These findings are consistent with severe sleep-disordered breathing. Further evaluation and treatment planning are recommended.

Sleep Medicine Consultation
Date: 07/29/2026
Patient: Shaunna McClure, 67-year-old female

Reason for Consultation:
Evaluation and management of sleep-related issues.

History:
Ms. McClure presents for follow-up regarding her sleep apnea treatment. She has been using CPAP therapy but reports difficulty tolerating the device.

Physical Examination:
BMI 27.9 kg/m2.

Assessment:
The patient demonstrates CPAP intolerance: download shows average use 1.8 hours per night on 24% of nights despite mask refitting; shared decision-making with the patient documented that CPAP is not tolerated.

Plan:
Discuss alternative treatment options for sleep apnea including oral appliance therapy and positional therapy. Recommend follow-up sleep study if symptoms persist or worsen. Continue monitoring and supportive care.

Follow-up:
Schedule return visit in 3 months or sooner if symptoms change.
